translations.answer: Maintainer points out two clear risks: using real joint states in the lower-level joint position controller and feeding it back in the TSID again would create double feedback. The original code uses q_real and v_real to compute a_sol, but starts integrating from a different set of virtual q_tsid and v_tsid, leading to mismatched state and acceleration. He states he is unaware of a clean, general solution for this structure, and a clean path is joint torque control. If the hardware can only perform position control, the thread support boundary is not to directly repeat the real joint states in the closed-loop.
translations.applicability: Applicable to the outer output position of TSID, and different closed-loop structure for force-torque control interface in the robot's lower-level PID architecture.
translations.credibility.rationale: Environmental, processing steps, and results have engineering records, but formal cross-validation or independent replication is missing.
translations.details.attempts.0: Maintainer provides virtual state open-loop TSID and torque control boundaries; practitioner shares model state TSID with foot F/T/IMU stabilizer; questioner attempts real floating base, Cartesian end-effector error integration, contact reference, and gain adjustment.
translations.details.diagnostics.0: Distinguish between QP state, integral start point, and base position feedback for PID; verify that a_sol corresponds to q_real but integrates from q_tsid.
translations.details.diagnostics.1: Confirm if joint feedback is handled by the lower-level position servo loop; separate floating base/contact stability issues from joint position closed-loop.
translations.details.effective_fixes.0: A clean and general approach within threads is to use joint torque control; position control robots typically run TSID with virtual model states and adjust CoM using F/T or IMU stabilizers.
translations.details.effective_fixes.1: The user's specific real machine solution does not use true floating base states, and corrects the reference by recalculating end-effector poses based on real measured joint positions, with a small offset added to the hip and ankle joints after QP.
translations.details.environments.0: TSID; Gazebo with PyBullet; position control robot; practitioner cites iCub/Talos, questioner ultimately verifies on a real machine without specifying the model.
translations.details.limits.0: The maintainer explicitly states that they are unaware of directly feeding the true state into the clean general solution for TSID.
translations.details.limits.1: End-effector error integral and joint offset are claimed hacks by the questioner and should not be treated as general parameters for other robots.
translations.details.limits.2: Discussions on contact reference height, landing rebound, and swing/contact gain have not formed a unified rule confirmed by the maintainers.
translations.details.outcomes.0: The requester reported that the scheme works in simulation and on real hardware; no stable margin, parameter range, or cross-robot reproducibility was provided.
translations.details.problem_statements.0: Can a position control robot directly calculate the TSID QP using real joint/float base states, and then integrate from virtual states to obtain position commands?
translations.details.problem_statements.1: If the true state is not directly fed into the TSID, how can the real-time deviation enter the control loop?
translations.details.safety_notes.0: Safety boundaries for amplitude, speed, and integral saturation should be set before real-world application, and verified gradually in protected conditions; the original post did not provide these safety boundaries.
translations.details.suspected_causes.0: Real state enters both TSID and lower-level position controller, causing dual feedback.
translations.details.suspected_causes.1: The acceleration derived from the real state is inconsistent with the integral from the virtual state.
translations.details.symptoms.0: Only integrates virtual/command states and runs when using virtual/command states; task error calculation and QP are performed using real states, leading to system divergence quickly.
translations.details.symptoms.1: Real-time floating base ground truth or estimator state directly feedback still causes instability.
translations.details.symptoms.2: Significant tracking error at the groin and ankle joints during the weight shift phase.
translations.media_summaries.0: The author's comments include support foot reference/virtual pose curves and two landing video clips, and explain the blue-green curves, reference height, and rebound phenomenon; the card does not use image or video values for supplementation, and general conclusions are confirmed only through text.
translations.source.title: Directing real state to the TSID via a humanoid robot leads to dual feedback and inconsistent state
translations.terms.0: Task-Space Inverse Dynamics (TSID) (任务空间逆动力学)
translations.title: Why does position control in humanoid robots tend to diverge when directly feeding the true state into the TSID?
